docs.title: Documentation archived
docs.text:
The maintained operational documentation moved to TripSit/live, a private repository requiring TripSit infrastructure access:

  • docs/architecture.md
  • docs/networking.md
  • docs/storage-and-backups.md
  • docs/troubleshooting.md

The migration was verified on 16 November 2026 and saved in live commit f54111b. Runtime Docker inspection and restoration remain explicitly unverified; the maintained documents record the checks actually performed.

All original pages, site configuration, workflows, and Git history are preserved here. The historical pages below describe an older setup and must not be used as current operational instructions. Submit future infrastructure documentation changes to TripSit/live.

docs.title: TripSit Infrastructure Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to the official infrastructure and server documentation for TripSit Live.

This documentation site is designed for systems administrators, operators, and developers who are familiar with standard Ubuntu Linux system administration but may be new to the TripSit server deployment and Docker architecture.

docs.title: 🚀 Quick Start & Navigation
docs.text:
Whether you are onboarding as a new sysadmin or looking up a specific service configuration, here is where to start:

  • Architecture Overview — Understand the big picture: how network traffic flows, container isolation, and proxying work.
  • Host Deployment Guide — Step-by-step guide to preparing an Ubuntu server, configuring environment files, and launching services.
  • Core Infrastructure — Deep dive into Traefik, Docker Socket Proxy, CrowdSec, Fail2ban, and Portainer.
  • Services Catalog — Browse all hosted services: Chat & Bridges (IRC, Matrix, Revcord), Web & Bots (Tripbot, Website, Calculators), Knowledge (MediaWiki, Wiki.js, Moodle), and Monitoring Utilities.
  • Operations & Troubleshooting — Day-to-day commands, logs, backups, and emergency recovery procedures.

docs.title: 🎯 Key Design Goals
docs.text:
The TripSit live server infrastructure is built with four primary tenets:

  1. Security-First Architecture: Unrestricted socket exposure is disabled. All container access to Docker daemon is funneled through a fine-grained docker-socket-proxy. Intrusion prevention is enforced via Fail2ban, CrowdSec, and Traefik bouncers.
  2. Automated Reverse Proxy & SSL: Traefik handles HTTP/HTTPS routing dynamically via Docker container labels and automatically provisions Let's Encrypt TLS certificates.
  3. Modular Composable Services: Services are decoupled into logical docker-compose.<name>.yml files (e.g., docker-compose.core.yml, docker-compose.tripbot.yml, docker-compose.matrix.yml), allowing independent deployment and updates.
  4. Data Isolation: Application runtime configurations, data databases, logs, and secrets are mapped cleanly to standard host paths under /docker/.

docs.title: 💡 Prerequisite Knowledge
docs.text:
To operate this environment efficiently, you should be comfortable with: - Standard Ubuntu CLI commands (systemctl, journalctl, chmod/chown, ufw, ss/netstat). - Basic Docker concepts (containers, images, volumes, bridge networks). - Basic networking concepts (DNS records, A/AAAA records, TCP/UDP ports, reverse proxying).

No prior knowledge of TripSit's internal tools is required—every container and configuration file is explained step-by-step in this documentation!

docs.title: Container Management & CI/CD
docs.text: This section details the management infrastructure, container maintenance, log monitoring, automated updates, backups, and continuous integration pipelines on TripSit Live.

docs.title: 🐳 1. Container Management (Portainer)
docs.text:
Portainer provides a GUI management console for monitoring container health, viewing container logs, inspecting volume allocations, and managing Docker networks.

  • Container Name: portainer
  • Image: portainer/portainer-ee:latest
  • Socket Access: Connected via socket-net to socket-proxy:2375.
  • URL: https://portainer.tripsit.me (Protected by Google OAuth SSO).

docs.title: 📋 2. Real-Time Log Viewer (Dozzle)
docs.text:
Dozzle is a lightweight web application for streaming real-time container logs without needing SSH access.

  • Container Name: dozzle
  • Image: amir20/dozzle:latest
  • Socket Access: Connected to socket-proxy:2375.
  • URL: https://dozzle.tripsit.me (Protected by Google OAuth SSO).

docs.title: 🔄 3. Automated Container Updates (Watchtower)
docs.text: Watchtower monitors running Docker containers and automatically updates them when new images are published to registries.

docs.title: Selective Update Policy
docs.text:
To prevent unexpected breaking updates on production critical services, Watchtower updates are controlled explicitly via container labels:

labels:
  # Enable automatic updates for this container
  - com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true

  # Disable automatic updates (e.g. for database or breaking state services)
  - com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=false

docs.title: 🧹 4. Docker Garbage Collection (dockergc)
docs.text:
Over time, unused Docker images, dangling layers, and exited containers consume significant disk space.

  • Service: dockergc (clockworksoul/docker-gc-cron:latest).
  • Function: Runs on a automated cron schedule to prune dangling images, exited containers, and unused build caches.

docs.title: 💾 5. Backups & Disaster Recovery (Duplicati)
docs.text:
Duplicati manages automated, encrypted offsite backups for application configurations and databases.

  • Container Name: duplicati
  • Image: ghcr.io/linuxserver/duplicati:latest
  • Mounted Backup Sources:
  • /docker/appdata (Application state)
  • /docker/secrets (Service credentials)
  • URL: Protected behind Google OAuth SSO.

docs.title: 🚀 6. Continuous Integration & Deployment (Drone CI)
docs.text:
TripSit uses Drone CI for continuous integration and automated deployment builds.

  • Drone Server (drone): drone/drone:2 — Handles webhooks, user permissions, and deployment triggers.
  • Drone Runner (drone_runner): drone/drone-runner-docker:1 — Executes pipeline steps in isolated ephemeral Docker containers connected via socket-proxy.

docs.title: Security & Access Control
docs.text: This page covers the security mechanisms deployed across the TripSit server stack to protect infrastructure, isolate containers, detect threats, and enforce Single Sign-On (SSO).

docs.title: 🔒 1. Docker Socket Proxy (docker-socket-proxy)
docs.text: The Docker UNIX socket (/var/run/docker.sock) is the control plane for the Docker daemon. Providing unconfined access to /var/run/docker.sock allows any container to gain root access to the entire host machine.

docs.title: Security Architecture
docs.text:
TripSit uses tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy, an HAProxy-based security sidecar, to filter and restrict access to the Docker API.

┌──────────────────┐               ┌─────────────────────┐               ┌─────────────────┐
│ Container        │ API Request   │ docker-socket-proxy │ Read-only Unix  │ Docker Daemon   │
│ (Portainer, etc.)│──────────────►│ (TCP 127.0.0.1:2375)│────────────────►│ (/docker.sock)  │
└──────────────────┘               └─────────────────────┘               └─────────────────┘
                                              │
                                    Blocks Auth/Exec/Secrets

docs.title: Configuration Rules (docker-compose.core.yml)
docs.text:
docker-socket-proxy:
    image: tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy
    container_name: socket-proxy
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:2375:2375" # Exposed ONLY to local loopback/internal bridge network
    networks:
      - socket-net
    volumes:
      - /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock
    environment:
      # Granted permissions
      EVENTS: 1
      PING: 1
      VERSION: 1
      CONTAINERS: 1
      IMAGES: 1
      NETWORKS: 1
      SERVICES: 1
      VOLUMES: 1
      POST: 1       # Required by Watchtower
      BUILD: 1      # Required by Drone CI
      # Strictly revoked endpoints
      AUTH: 0
      SECRETS: 0
      COMMIT: 0
      CONFIGS: 0
      EXEC: 0       # Prevents arbitrary container execution via socket
      NODES: 0
      SWARM: 0

docs.title: Fail2ban (fail2ban)
docs.text:
Fail2ban scans system and container logs for brute-force patterns and dynamically manipulates host iptables firewall rules to drop offensive IPs.

  • Image: crazymax/fail2ban:latest
  • Network Mode: host with NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW Linux capabilities.
  • Monitored Logs: /docker/logs/fail2ban, /docker/logs/traefik.

docs.title: CrowdSec IPS & Traefik Bouncer (crowdsec, crowdsec_traefik)
docs.text:
CrowdSec is an open-source collaborative Intrusion Prevention System (IPS).

  • Database: Dedicated MariaDB container (crowdsec_db).
  • Collections: Configured with rule collections for Traefik, HTTP CVEs, Linux system logs, and iptables.
  • Traefik Bouncer: crowdsec_traefik integrates directly with Traefik as middleware. When CrowdSec flags an offending IP address globally or locally, the bouncer blocks the HTTP request at the Traefik router layer before it reaches any backend container.

docs.title: 🔑 3. Google OAuth Single Sign-On (oauth)
docs.text: Administrative web tools (Portainer, Dozzle logs, Netdata metrics, Duplicati backups) are protected behind Google OAuth SSO via thomseddon/traefik-forward-auth.

docs.title: How OAuth Forward Auth Middleware Works
docs.text:
1. An unauthenticated user attempts to visit https://portainer.tripsit.me.
  2. Traefik checks the container middleware label googleAuth@file.
  3. Traefik redirects the browser to https://oauth.tripsit.me/_oauth for Google authentication.
  4. If the user's email address is present in the OAUTH_WHITELIST environment variable, OAuth sets a secure encrypted cookie and grants access.
  5. If unauthorized, access is denied.
  oauth:
    image: thomseddon/traefik-forward-auth:latest
    container_name: oauth
    environment:
      - CLIENT_ID=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID}
      - CLIENT_SECRET=${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET}
      - SECRET=${OAUTH_SECRET}
      - COOKIE_DOMAIN=${DNS_DOMAIN}
      - WHITELIST=${OAUTH_WHITELIST}
      - DEFAULT_ACTION=auth
      - DEFAULT_PROVIDER=google

docs.title: 🔐 4. Keycloak Identity Management (keycloak)
docs.text: For advanced user identity management and single sign-on across TripSit platforms: - Service: keycloak (docker.io/bitnami/keycloak:21.1.2). - Database: keycloak_db (PostgreSQL 15.4). - Network: Private keycloak_db-net network isolated from public access.

docs.title: Traefik Reverse Proxy & DNS Integration
docs.text: This section explains how Traefik acts as the central ingress router for all web traffic targeting the TripSit live server infrastructure.

docs.title: 🎯 Role of Traefik
docs.text:
Traefik is a modern edge router / reverse proxy that automatically discovers containers running on Docker networks and routes HTTP/HTTPS requests to them based on dynamic configuration labels.

Key benefits in TripSit's architecture: - No Manual Nginx/Apache Routing Files: Service routes are defined directly in each service's docker-compose.<name>.yml using container labels. - Automated SSL/TLS Certificates: Obtains and automatically renews SSL certificates from Let's Encrypt via DNS-01 or HTTP-01 challenges. - Cloudflare Companion Integration: Automatically creates and updates Cloudflare DNS records when new containers with routing labels are created.

docs.title: ⚙️ Core Traefik Service Breakdown
docs.text:
In docker-compose.core.yml:

  traefik:
    image: traefik:latest
    container_name: traefik
    ports:
      - "80:80"     # HTTP entrypoint (redirects to 443)
      - "443:443"   # HTTPS entrypoint
    networks:
      - traefik-net
      - socket-net
    environment:
      - CF_API_EMAIL=${CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL}
      - CF_API_KEY=${CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY}
    volumes:
      - ${DOCKERDIR}/traefik/acme.json:/acme.json
      - ${DOCKERDIR}/traefik/traefik.yml:/etc/traefik/traefik.yml:ro
      - ${DOCKERDIR}/traefik/rules:/rules:ro

docs.title: 🏷️ How Traefik Container Labels Work
docs.text: When adding a new web container to any compose file, Traefik routes traffic to it using standard labels.

docs.title: Standard Label Template:
docs.text:
labels:
  - com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.enable=true
  - traefik.enable=true
  - traefik.docker.network=traefik-net
  - traefik.http.routers.<service_name>.rule=Host(`subdomain.${DNS_DOMAIN}`)
  - traefik.http.routers.<service_name>.entrypoints=websecure
  - traefik.http.routers.<service_name>.tls.certresolver=letsencrypt
  - traefik.http.services.<service_name>-svc.loadbalancer.server.port=8080

docs.title: Explanation of Key Labels:
docs.text:
• traefik.enable=true: Tells Traefik to expose this container.
  • traefik.docker.network=traefik-net: Specifies which network Traefik should use to reach the container.
  • traefik.http.routers.<service_name>.rule: Defines the rule for matching incoming HTTP requests (e.g. Host matching, path prefix matching).
  • traefik.http.routers.<service_name>.entrypoints: Specifies entrypoint (websecure for HTTPS / port 443).
  • traefik.http.routers.<service_name>.tls.certresolver: Directs Traefik to use the configured Let's Encrypt certificate resolver.
  • traefik.http.services.<service_name>-svc.loadbalancer.server.port: Explicitly declares which container internal port receives traffic.

docs.title: 🌐 Cloudflare Companion (cloudflare_companion)
docs.text:
In docker-compose.core.yml: 

  cloudflare_companion:
    image: tiredofit/traefik-cloudflare-companion:latest
    container_name: cloudflare_companion
    environment:
      - TIMEZONE=${TZ}
      - TRAEFIK_VERSION=2
      - CF_EMAIL=${CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL}
      - CF_TOKEN=${CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY}
      - TARGET_DOMAIN=${DNS_DOMAIN}
      - DOMAIN1=${DNS_DOMAIN}

docs.title: How Cloudflare Companion Works:
docs.text:
1. Listens to Docker container state events via socket-proxy.
  2. Inspects Host(...) rules in new container labels.
  3. Automatically creates a CNAME or A record in Cloudflare pointing to the server's public IP address.
  4. Removes DNS records when containers are destroyed.

docs.title: 🔑 Traefik SSL Exporter (ssl_export)
docs.text:
In docker-compose.irc.yml: 

  ssl_export:
    image: rafi0101/traefik-ssl-certificate-exporter
    container_name: ssl_export
    volumes:
      - ${DOCKERDIR}/traefik/acme.json:/acme.json:ro
      - ${DOCKERDIR}/certs:/output:rw

docs.title: Purpose:
docs.text:
Traefik stores certificates in a single JSON file (acme.json). Non-Traefik native services—such as the Ergo IRC daemon—require standard .crt and .key PEM files on disk.

ssl_export monitors acme.json and automatically extracts certificates into standard PEM files inside ${DOCKERDIR}/certs/ whenever Traefik renews a certificate.

docs.title: Host Deployment Guide
docs.text: This guide walks an Ubuntu Linux administrator step-by-step through configuring a host machine and deploying the TripSit server stack.

docs.title: 📋 System Requirements
docs.text:
• Operating System: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or 24.04 LTS (64-bit).
  • CPU: 4+ cores recommended.
  • RAM: 16 GB+ recommended (given Matrix, Sonar, Moodle, and PostgreSQL instances).
  • Disk: 100 GB+ SSD/NVMe storage mounted at / or /docker.
  • Public IP: Static IPv4 address (and optionally IPv6).

docs.title: 1. Update Package Index and Install Dependencies
docs.text:
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y curl git ufw jq ca-certificates gnupg lsbrelease

docs.title: 2. Install Docker Engine & Docker Compose Plugin
docs.text:
Install the official Docker repository on Ubuntu: 

# Add Docker's official GPG key:
sudo install -m 0755 -d /etc/apt/keyrings
sudo curl -fsSL https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu/gpg -o /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc
sudo chmod a+r /etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc

# Add the repository to Apt sources:
echo \
  "deb [arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) signed-by=/etc/apt/keyrings/docker.asc] https://download.docker.com/linux/ubuntu \
  $(. /etc/os-release && echo "$VERSION_CODENAME") stable" | \
  sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/docker.list > /dev/null

sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y docker-ce docker-ce-cli containerd.io docker-buildx-plugin docker-compose-plugin

Verify installation: 

docker --version
docker compose version

docs.title: 📁 Step 2: Create Host Directory Structure
docs.text:
As described in the Architecture Overview, TripSit relies on specific paths under /docker.

Execute as root or with sudo: 

sudo mkdir -p /docker/appdata
sudo mkdir -p /docker/custom
sudo mkdir -p /docker/logs
sudo mkdir -p /docker/scripts
sudo mkdir -p /docker/secrets
sudo mkdir -p /docker/shared

# Lock down secrets folder permissions
sudo chmod 700 /docker/secrets

docs.title: 🔑 Step 3: Global Environment Setup (.env)
docs.text:
Each compose stack references global system and environment variables stored in a central .env file located in the root repository folder (/home/moonbear/UAT/.env or working directory).

Security Rule

Never commit .env files to git repositories. Always use sample placeholders when creating configuration templates.

docs.title: Example Environment Configuration Template (.env)
docs.text:
Create a .env file in your repository root with the following parameters:

# System Parameters
TZ=UTC
PUID=1000
PGID=1000
DOCKERDIR=/docker

# Domain Setup
DNS_DOMAIN=tripsit.me
BOT_DOMAIN=tripsit.me

# Authentication / OAuth
GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=<your-google-client-id>.apps.googleusercontent.com
GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=<your-google-client-secret>
OAUTH_SECRET=<random-32-byte-secret>
OAUTH_WHITELIST=user1@example.com,user2@example.com

# Cloudflare Integration
CLOUDFLARE_EMAIL=admin@tripsit.me
CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY=<your-cloudflare-api-key>

# Database Passwords
CROWDSEC_DB_PASS=<secure-password>
TRIPBOT_DB_PASS=<secure-password>
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=<secure-password>
MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD=<secure-password>

docs.title: 🚀 Step 4: Launching Docker Compose Stacks
docs.text: TripSit services are launched modularly using standard docker compose commands specifying the target .yml file.

docs.title: 1. Launch Core Infrastructure (Crucial First Step!)
docs.text:
Core infrastructure (Traefik, Socket Proxy, OAuth) must be running before dependent stacks start:

# Navigate to repository directory
cd /home/moonbear/UAT

# Validate compose syntax
docker compose -f docker-compose.core.yml config

# Start core services in detached mode
docker compose -f docker-compose.core.yml up -d

Check running containers: 

docker compose -f docker-compose.core.yml ps

docs.title: 2. Launch Administrative Applications
docs.text: docker compose -f docker-compose.apps.yml up -d

docs.title: 3. Launch Communication & Chat Services
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose.irc.yml up -d
docker compose -f docker-compose.matrix.yml up -d

docs.title: 4. Launch Web, Bots & Knowledge Bases
docs.text:
docker compose -f docker-compose.tripbot.yml up -d
docker compose -f docker-compose.website.yml up -d
docker compose -f docker-compose.wiki.yml up -d

docs.title: 🛡️ Step 5: Firewall Setup (UFW)
docs.text:
Ensure standard Ubuntu UFW rules allow required inbound ports:

# Allow SSH
sudo ufw allow 22/tcp

# Allow Web (Traefik)
sudo ufw allow 80/tcp
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp

# Allow IRC (if running public Ergo IRC)
sudo ufw allow 6667/tcp
sudo ufw allow 6697/tcp

# Allow Wireguard VPN (if enabled)
sudo ufw allow 51820/udp

# Enable UFW
sudo ufw enable
sudo ufw status verbose

docs.title: 🔄 Updating & Restarting Services
docs.text:
To pull updated container images and restart a stack gracefully:

docker compose -f docker-compose.apps.yml pull
docker compose -f docker-compose.apps.yml up -d --remove-orphans

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text: This page provides a high-level conceptual overview of the TripSit live server environment, networking layout, and security architecture.

docs.title: 🏗️ High-Level System Architecture
docs.text:
TripSit Live operates on a modular Docker Compose stack running on Ubuntu Linux. Rather than putting every service into a single monolithic compose file, the infrastructure is split across targeted stack files.

                  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │                 Internet                     │
                  └──────────────────────┬───────────────────────┘
                                         │
                                   Ports 80 / 443
                                         │
                                         ▼
                  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐
                  │           Traefik Reverse Proxy              │
                  │   (Automatic TLS via Let's Encrypt / DNS)    │
                  └━━━━━━┬━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┬━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━┬━━━━━━━┘
                         │               │               │
      ┌──────────────────┴──┐  ┌─────────┴─────────┐  ┌──┴────────────────┐
      │ Core Infrastructure │  │   Chat & Bridges  │  │  Web, Bots & Apps  │
      │  - Socket Proxy     │  │  - Ergo IRC       │  │  - Tripbot API     │
      │  - CrowdSec / F2B   │  │  - Synapse Matrix │  │  - Main Website    │
      │  - OAuth / Keycloak │  │  - Element Web    │  │  - MediaWiki       │
      │  - Portainer        │  │  - Revcord Bridge │  │  - Calculators     │
      └─────────────────────┘  └───────────────────┘  └────────────────────┘

docs.title: 1. External Traffic Entry
docs.text:
• Port 80 (HTTP): Traffic on HTTP is automatically redirected to HTTPS (Port 443) by Traefik.
  • Port 443 (HTTPS): All web services are routed through Traefik using Host-based routing labels defined on individual containers (e.g. Host(\wiki.tripsit.me`)`).
  • Direct Service Ports: Select non-HTTP services expose dedicated host ports (e.g., SSH on port 22, Ergo IRC on 6667/6697, Stalwart Mail on 25/587/465/143/993, Wireguard on 51820 UDP).

docs.title: 2. Internal Docker Networks
docs.text: Every compose stack defines isolated internal docker networks (e.g., traefik-net, socket-net, tripbot_database-net, matrix_db-net). - Network Isolation: Backend databases (PostgreSQL, MariaDB) exist on private networks accessible only by their respective application containers. - Proxy Network (traefik-net): Traefik joins the traefik-net network to forward incoming web requests to application containers without exposing internal application ports directly to the host host interface.

docs.title: 1. Docker Socket Proxy (socket-proxy)
docs.text:
Critical Security Requirement

Directly mounting the Docker socket (/var/run/docker.sock) into containers gives root-equivalent host privileges.

To eliminate this vulnerability: - The host Unix socket is disabled for standard application containers. - A hardened tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy container listens on an isolated internal network (socket-net). - Containers like Traefik, Portainer, and Watchtower query socket-proxy with strict read-only or minimal permission flags set via environment variables.

docs.title: 2. Intrusion Detection & Prevention
docs.text:
• Fail2ban: Monitors log files for brute-force attacks and dynamically updates firewall rules.
  • CrowdSec: Analyzes ingress web logs via Traefik bouncers to block known malicious IP addresses collaboratively across community threat intelligence.
  • Traefik Forward Auth (Google OAuth): Protects administrative dashboards (Portainer, Dozzle, Netdata, Duplicati) behind Google Single Sign-On (SSO).

docs.title: 📁 Storage & Host Layout
docs.text:
All persistent application data, custom Dockerfiles, logs, and secrets reside under a standardized host hierarchy:

Host Directory Description Access Permission /docker/appdata/ Persistent volumes for application state (databases, configs, uploads) Service-specific /docker/custom/ Custom Dockerfile build contexts for TripSit apps Root / Operator /docker/logs/ Centralized log folder mounted by containers Read/Write /docker/secrets/ Credentials, API tokens, and certificate files Root only (0600/0700) /docker/scripts/ Maintenance, maintenance automation, and health check scripts Operator

docs.title: 📦 Stack Breakdown
docs.text:
The system is organized into distinct compose files:

  • docker-compose.core.yml: Traefik, Socket Proxy, CrowdSec, Fail2ban, OAuth, Portainer, Duplicati, Drone, Keycloak.
  • docker-compose.apps.yml: Admin utilities (Dozzle, Netdata, Filebrowser, IT-tools, Uptime Kuma, Wireguard, SonarQube, Trilium).
  • docker-compose.tripbot.yml: Tripbot discord bot, production API, database, pgAdmin, and staging deployment.
  • docker-compose.website.yml: Main TripSit website container stack.
  • docker-compose.irc.yml: Ergo IRC server and Traefik SSL exporter.
  • docker-compose.matrix.yml: Synapse Matrix homeserver, Element Web client, Matrix Admin, Coturn TURN server, Redis, Postgres.
  • docker-compose.wiki.yml / wikijs.yml / drugwikijs.yml: Knowledge base mediawiki & Wiki.js stacks.
  • docker-compose.moodle.yml: Moodle learning platform (learn.tripsit.me).
  • docker-compose.stalwart.yml: Stalwart mail server.

docs.title: Directory Layout & Host Volume Mounts
docs.text: This section describes the filesystem layout on the host server under /docker and explains how container data persistence is maintained across restarts and upgrades.

docs.title: 📂 Host Directory Hierarchy (/docker)
docs.text:
All persistent data for containers is located under /docker on the host Ubuntu filesystem:

/docker/
├── appdata/        # Application state, databases, config files
├── custom/         # Custom Dockerfiles and build contexts
├── fail2ban/       # Fail2ban configuration data
├── logs/           # Centralized log storage mounted by services
├── scripts/        # Operational shell scripts and cron tasks
├── secrets/        # Encrypted passwords, keys, and API credentials
└── shared/         # Shared assets used across multiple containers

docs.title: 🗄️ Application Data Breakdown (/docker/appdata)
docs.text:
Each service has a dedicated directory inside /docker/appdata/ to keep data isolated:

Directory Container Owner Contents & Description /docker/appdata/traefik/ traefik Traefik dynamic rules, traefik.yml, and acme.json SSL certificates. /docker/appdata/portainer/ portainer Portainer database and application configuration. /docker/appdata/crowdsec/ crowdsec CrowdSec hub configurations, bouncer keys, and threat database. /docker/appdata/matrix/ matrix_synapse Synapse media store, server keys, and configuration. /docker/appdata/moodle/ moodle Moodle uploads, courses, and LMS data. /docker/appdata/wiki/ wiki MediaWiki upload directory and LocalSettings.php. /docker/appdata/wikijs/ wikijs Wiki.js file assets and configuration. /docker/appdata/tripbot/ tripbot Tripbot application logs, dynamic assets, and database dumps. /docker/appdata/uptime-kuma/ kuma SQLite database storing status checks and uptime statistics. /docker/appdata/netdata/ netdata Netdata metric history and database.

docs.title: 🏗️ Custom Docker Build Contexts (/docker/custom)
docs.text:
Services that use build/custom image specifications store their Dockerfile and build source files under /docker/custom/:

  • /docker/custom/tripbot/ — Build context for custom Tripbot container image.
  • /docker/custom/website/ — Build context for main website container image.
  • /docker/custom/calculator_benzos/ — Build context for benzo calculator app.
  • /docker/custom/calculator_volume/ — Build context for volume calculator app.

docs.title: 🪵 Log Directory Layout (/docker/logs)
docs.text:
Log files generated by containers are mounted to /docker/logs/ so host monitoring services (such as Fail2ban and CrowdSec) can read them:

  • /docker/logs/fail2ban/ — Monitored by fail2ban service.
  • /docker/logs/crowdsec/ — Web access logs parsed by crowdsec.
  • /docker/logs/traefik/ — Traefik access and error logs.
  • /docker/logs/nginx/ — Nginx access logs.

docs.title: 🔐 Security Permissions Guardrails
docs.text:
To prevent unauthorized access or privilege escalation:

# Ensure /docker/secrets is owned by root and readable only by root (0700)
sudo chown -R root:root /docker/secrets
sudo chmod 700 /docker/secrets

# Ensure log directory allows container log writes
sudo chmod 755 /docker/logs

docs.title: Maintenance & Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: This guide provides practical administrative procedures, useful shell commands, and troubleshooting workflows for managing TripSit Live.

docs.title: 🛠️ Essential Management Commands
docs.text: All container management should be performed from the root directory of the repository (/home/moonbear/UAT) where compose files and .env live.

docs.title: 1. View Service Status
docs.text:
# View status of core services
docker compose -f docker-compose.core.yml ps

# View all containers running on the host
docker ps -a --format "table {{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}\t{{.Ports}}"

docs.title: 2. View Real-Time Logs
docs.text:
# Follow logs for Traefik
docker compose -f docker-compose.core.yml logs -f traefik

# Follow logs for Tripbot
docker compose -f docker-compose.tripbot.yml logs -f tripbot

# Follow logs for a specific container by name
docker logs -f --tail 100 matrix_synapse

docs.title: 3. Restart a Specific Service Stack
docs.text:
# Restart core stack without affecting other stacks
docker compose -f docker-compose.core.yml restart

# Force recreate a single container after updating configuration
docker compose -f docker-compose.tripbot.yml up -d --force-recreate tripbot

docs.title: 🔄 Updating Stack Services
docs.text:
To update services safely to their latest docker images:

# Step 1: Pull updated images for target stack
docker compose -f docker-compose.apps.yml pull

# Step 2: Recreate containers with new images (downtime < 2 seconds)
docker compose -f docker-compose.apps.yml up -d --remove-orphans

# Step 3: Prune unused old image layers
docker image prune -f

docs.title: Scenario A: Traefik Returns "404 Not Found" for a Domain
docs.text:
1. Verify Dynamic Routing Label: Ensure container has traefik.enable=true and traefik.http.routers.<name>.rule=Host(...) labels.
  2. Check Container Network: Container MUST be connected to traefik-net.
  3. Inspect Traefik Dashboard / Logs: 
    docker logs traefik --tail 50 | grep -i error

docs.title: Scenario B: Database Connection Errors in Container
docs.text:
1. Check Database Network: Application containers must share a common docker network with their database container (e.g. moodle-net & moodle_data-net).
  2. Verify Environment Passwords: Confirm .env database passwords match application config files.
  3. Check Database Container Status: 
    docker ps | grep db
docker logs tripbot_database --tail 50

docs.title: Scenario C: Socket Proxy Permission Denied Errors
docs.text: If Portainer, Watchtower, or Traefik complain about Docker API access: 1. Verify docker-socket-proxy container is running (docker ps | grep socket-proxy). 2. Verify target container environment variable DOCKER_HOST is set to tcp://socket-proxy:2375. 3. Check docker-socket-proxy environment flags in docker-compose.core.yml to confirm the required endpoint (e.g. CONTAINERS: 1, POST: 1) is granted (1).

docs.title: 1. Manual Backup of PostgreSQL (e.g., Tripbot Database)
docs.text: docker exec -t tripbot_database pg_dump -U postgres tripbot > /docker/appdata/tripbot/tripbot_backup_$(date +%F).sql

docs.title: 2. Manual Restore of PostgreSQL
docs.text: cat /docker/appdata/tripbot/tripbot_backup.sql | docker exec -i tripbot_database psql -U postgres -d tripbot

docs.title: 3. Manual Backup of MariaDB (e.g., MediaWiki Database)
docs.text: docker exec -t wiki_db mysqldump -u root -p"${MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD}" wiki > /docker/appdata/wiki/wiki_backup_$(date +%F).sql

docs.title: 🧹 System Cleanup & Disk Maintenance
docs.text:
Check disk usage across Docker containers, images, and volumes: 

docker system df

Prune stopped containers, unused networks, and dangling images: 

docker system prune -f

Prune unused data volumes (Use with caution—ensure no persistent data volumes are orphan!): 

docker volume prune

docs.title: Bots & Web Applications
docs.text: This section documents TripSit's core application ecosystem, including the flagship Tripbot service, the main web portal, and harm reduction tools.

docs.title: 🤖 1. Tripbot Ecosystem (docker-compose.tripbot.yml)
docs.text:
Tripbot is TripSit's primary Discord bot and harm-reduction assistant. It provides drug interaction lookup, dosage information, harm-reduction guides, and community support workflows.

                         ┌──────────────────────────┐
                         │   Discord / Web Clients  │
                         └────────────┬─────────────┘
                                      │
                                HTTPS / API
                                      │
                                      ▼
┌───────────────────────┐   ┌───────────────────┐   ┌───────────────────────┐
│ Tripbot Bot & API     │──►│ PostgreSQL DB     │◄──│ pgAdmin4 Dashboard    │
│ (container: tripbot)  │   │ (tripbot_database)│   │ (tripbot_pgadmin)     │
└───────────────────────┘   └───────────────────┘   └───────────────────────┘

docs.title: Components Breakdown
docs.text: Container Name Image / Context Purpose & Routing tripbot custom/build Core Tripbot bot instance and public REST API server (api.tripsit.me). tripbot_database postgres:15.4 Production PostgreSQL database storing user preferences, bot settings, and logs. tripbot_deploy custom/build Staging/development deployment runner (tripbot-deploy.tripsit.me). tripbot_database_deploy postgres:15.4 Staging PostgreSQL database. tripbot_pgadmin dpage/pgadmin4:latest Web-based database management interface (database.tripsit.me, pgadmin.tripsit.me).

docs.title: 🌐 2. Main TripSit Website (docker-compose.website.yml)
docs.text:
• Container Name: website
  • Build Context: Custom build (/docker/custom/website or workspace repository).
  • Networks: website-net connected to Traefik.
  • Routing Rules:
  • Host(\tripsit.me`)`
  • Host(\chat.tripsit.me`)`
  • Host(\drugs.tripsit.me`)`
  • Host(\support.tripsit.me`)`

The main web application serves public harm reduction resources, drug factsheet search interfaces, and direct links to IRC and Matrix chat rooms.

docs.title: 🧮 3. Harm Reduction Calculators (docker-compose.apps.yml)
docs.text: TripSit hosts standalone interactive calculators to assist users in dosage safety and volumetric measurement:

docs.title: Benzodiazepine Equivalence Calculator (calculator_benzos)
docs.text:
• Container Name: calculator_benzos
  • Build Context: custom/build
  • Purpose: Calculates dosage equivalencies across common benzodiazepine compounds to reduce accidental overdose risks.

docs.title: Volumetric Liquid Dosing Calculator (calculator_volume)
docs.text:
• Container Name: calculator_volume
  • Build Context: custom/build
  • Purpose: Calculates precise liquid volume concentrations for accurate micro-dosing and volumetric administration safety.

docs.title: Chat & Bridge Services
docs.text: TripSit operates a multi-platform communication suite, uniting IRC, Matrix, Discord, Revolt, and Stoat communities via real-time relay bridges.

docs.title: 💬 1. IRC Infrastructure (Ergo IRC)
docs.text:
TripSit's IRC network runs on Ergo, a modern IRC server written in Go with full IRCv3 support.

  • Compose File: docker-compose.irc.yml
  • Container Name: irc
  • Image: ghcr.io/ergochat/ergo:stable
  • Exposed Host Ports:
  • 6667: Standard plaintext IRC port.
  • 6697: Secure TLS IRC port.
  • SSL Certificates: Certificate files are generated by Traefik dynamically and synced to disk via the ssl_export sidecar.

docs.title: 🟢 2. Matrix Communications Stack
docs.text:
Matrix provides decentralized, end-to-end encrypted chat capabilities.

  • Compose File: docker-compose.matrix.yml
Container Name Image Purpose Public URL / Rule matrix_synapse matrixdotorg/synapse:latest Matrix Homeserver daemon matrix.tripsit.me matrix_webchat vectorim/element-web:latest Element Web Client element.tripsit.me matrix_admin awesometechnologies/synapse-admin Web GUI for Synapse server administration matrix-admin.tripsit.me matrix_voicechat coturn/coturn:latest Coturn STUN/TURN server for Matrix VoIP calls Internal / TURN ports matrix_db bitnami/postgresql:15.4.0 High-performance PostgreSQL database for Synapse Private matrix_db-net matrix_redis bitnami/redis:latest Cache layer for Matrix event replication Private matrix_redis-net

docs.title: Revcord Bridge (revcord)
docs.text:
• Location: /home/moonbear/UAT/revcord
  • Description: A TypeScript bridge using revolt.js that connects Discord and Revolt servers in real-time.
  • Capabilities: Message relay, attachment bridge, replies, embeds, edits, and deletions.
  • Database: SQLite (revcord.sqlite).

docs.title: Lightning Bridge (lightning / stoat)
docs.text:
• Location: /home/moonbear/UAT/lightning & docker-compose.stoat.yml
  • Description: A high-performance Go-based multi-platform bot and bridge system designed to connect Discord, Stoat, Matrix, Spacebar, and Telegram.
  • Database: Dedicated PostgreSQL database (lightning_database).

docs.title: Matterbridge (matterbridge)
docs.text:
• Image: 42wim/matterbridge:stable
  • Description: Relays chat messages across legacy IRC channels, Discord, and Matrix chatrooms.

docs.title: ✉️ 4. Mail Server (Stalwart)
docs.text:
• Compose File: docker-compose.stalwart.yml
  • Container Name: stalwart-mail
  • Image: stalwartlabs/stalwart:latest
  • Host Ports: 25 (SMTP), 587 (Submission), 465 (SMTPS), 143 (IMAP), 993 (IMAPS), 110 (POP3), 995 (POP3S), 4190 (ManageSieve).
  • Public Router Rule: mail.tripsit.io

docs.title: Monitoring & Utility Services
docs.text: This page documents the auxiliary tools, server performance monitoring systems, error tracking applications, and utility containers running on the server.

docs.title: Netdata (netdata)
docs.text:
• Image: netdata/netdata
  • Purpose: Real-time performance monitoring (CPU, RAM, disk I/O, network bandwidth, container utilization).
  • Security: Access is protected behind Google OAuth SSO (netdata.tripsit.me).

docs.title: Uptime Kuma (kuma)
docs.text:
• Image: louislam/uptime-kuma
  • Purpose: Uptime monitoring tool for HTTP endpoints, TCP ports, ping checks, and DNS records. Sends notifications (via Gotify / Discord) if a service goes down.
  • URL: kuma.tripsit.me

docs.title: Glitchtip Error Tracking (docker-compose.glitchtip.yml)
docs.text:
Glitchtip is an open-source, Sentry-compatible error logging application. It collects stack traces and runtime exception reports from Tripbot, websites, and custom microservices.

  • Web Service: glitchtip_web (glitchtip/glitchtip, Port 8000).
  • Worker & Migration: glitchtip_worker, glitchtip_migrate.
  • Database & Cache: glitchtip_postgres (PostgreSQL 15), glitchtip_redis (Redis).

docs.title: SonarQube Code Analysis (sonar)
docs.text:
• Image: sonarqube:community
  • Database: sonar_db (bitnami/postgresql:15.4.0)
  • Purpose: Automated static code analysis, code quality metrics, and security vulnerability scanning for TripSit codebases.

docs.title: 📁 3. File Management & Remote Access (Filebrowser, SFTP, Wireguard)
Filebrowser (filebrowser)
docs.text:
• Image: filebrowser/filebrowser:s6
  • Purpose: Web-based interface to manage files within /docker/appdata.

docs.title: SFTP Service (ftp)
docs.text:
• Image: atmoz/sftp:latest
  • Exposed Host Port: 2222:22
  • Purpose: Secure file transfer for authorized sysadmins.

docs.title: Wireguard VPN (wireguard)
docs.text:
• Image: ghcr.io/wg-easy/wg-easy
  • Exposed Host Ports: 51820:51820/udp, 51821:51821/tcp

docs.title: IT-Tools (it-tools)
docs.text:
• Image: corentinth/it-tools
  • Purpose: Collection of web-based developer utility tools (hash generators, regex testers, UUID generators, base64 converters).

docs.title: Trilium Notes (trilium)
docs.text:
• Image: zadam/trilium:0.63.1-beta
  • Purpose: Hierarchical note-taking application for internal system architecture notes, runbooks, and operational guides.

docs.title: Stationeers Server (stationeers)
docs.text:
• Compose File: docker-compose.stationeers.yml
  • Ports: 8443:8443, 27015-27016 (UDP/TCP).

docs.title: Factorio Dedicated Server (factorio)
docs.text:
• Compose File: docker-compose.apps.yml
  • Ports: 34197:34197/udp, 27015:27015/tcp.

docs.title: Knowledge Bases & Educational Platforms
docs.text: TripSit maintains multiple knowledge bases, community wikis, and an online learning management system (LMS) to curate drug education and harm reduction guides.

docs.title: 📚 1. TripSit MediaWiki (docker-compose.wiki.yml)
docs.text:
MediaWiki powers TripSit's primary public encyclopedia of substances, harm reduction guides, and safety protocols.

  • Stack Components:
  • wiki / mediawiki: Runs MediaWiki (bitnami/mediawiki:1.41.1 or standard mediawiki:latest).
  • wiki_db: MariaDB database storing wiki pages, revisions, user accounts, and category links.
  • Public Domain: https://wiki.tripsit.me
  • Container Ports:
  • Reverse proxied via Traefik.
  • Fallback internal host port: 8080:80.

docs.title: 📖 2. Wiki.js & DrugWikiJS
docs.text: TripSit operates Wiki.js instances for modern, markdown-based documentation and collaborative drug factsheets.

docs.title: Main Wiki.js Stack (docker-compose.wikijs.yml)
docs.text:
• Application Container: wikijs (ghcr.io/requarks/wiki:2)
  • Database: wikijs_db (postgres:15)
  • Domain: https://wiki2.tripsit.me

docs.title: DrugWikiJS Stack (docker-compose.drugwikijs.yml)
docs.text:
• Application Container: drugwikijs (ghcr.io/requarks/wiki:2)
  • Database: drugwikijs_db (postgres:14)
  • Purpose: Specialized factsheet repository focused specifically on chemical compounds, trip reports, and pharmacology metadata.

docs.title: 🎓 3. Moodle Learning Platform (docker-compose.moodle.yml)
docs.text:
TripSit operates Moodle, an open-source Learning Management System (LMS), to provide structured education courses for volunteers, trip-sitters, and community members.

  • Application Container: moodle (bitnami/moodle:4.5.3)
  • Database Container: moodle_db_maria (bitnami/mariadb:11.3.2)
  • Public Domain: https://learn.tripsit.me
  • Data Persistence: Mounts /docker/appdata/moodle and /docker/appdata/moodledata.

docs.title: 📰 4. WordPress Community Updates (docker-compose.wordpress.yml)
docs.text:
• Application Container: wordpress (wordpress:latest)
  • Database Container: wordpress_db (linuxserver/mariadb:latest)
  • Public Domain: https://updates.tripsit.me
  • Purpose: News blog, announcement posts, and community updates.
